program_title: Electrical and Computer Engineering (MASc, Co-op Available)
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Faculty of Engineering
notes: Thesis-based MASc, 2 years, requires 4 graduate half-courses (2+ at 700-level) plus thesis. Department research areas explicitly include Microelectronics and VLSI, Integrated/Embedded/Interconnected Systems, Power Electronics & Electric Machines, Signal Processing, Communications, Networks (Centre for Research in Micro- and Nano-systems). International admission not stated on this specific program page, but confirmed via McMaster's university-wide graduate international admissions pathway (global.mcmaster.ca/students and School of Graduate Studies international applicant procedures, gs.mcmaster.ca) which is a standard, well-established admissions route -- McMaster enrolls large numbers of international graduate students across ECE. Recommend a final direct check of gs.mcmaster.ca program-specific international requirements page before relying on this for a final decision.

program_title: Electrical and Computer Engineering (MEng, Co-op Available)
department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Faculty of Engineering
notes: Course-based MEng, 16 months, 7 graduate half-courses or equivalent. Same department/research areas as the MASc listed above (Microelectronics/VLSI, embedded systems, power electronics, etc., selectable via course specialization) -- tier guess B because it is a general coursework ECE degree rather than a VLSI/embedded-specific program. International admission confirmed the same way as the MASc entry above (university-wide international graduate admissions route, not a program-specific statement) -- verify directly before finalizing.

program_title: Maitrise es sciences appliquees (M.Sc.A.) - Genie electrique
notes: 2-year, 45-credit thesis-based M.Sc.A. in electrical engineering (30 credits thesis, 9 credits of 3 mandatory courses, 6 credits directed study in specialization). General EE program, no explicit VLSI/microelectronics specialization found, so tier B. International admission confirmed at university level: Universite de Moncton documentation explicitly addresses international/foreign students needing a study permit (CAQ+study permit process described in umce.umoncton.ca/international and the faculty's graduate admission documents), and the university is marketed as among the lowest-tuition Canadian universities for international students. Program taught in French; English proficiency not the relevant language requirement -- French proficiency would be required instead. Official faculty page (umcm-ingenierie-electrique) should be checked directly for the current graduate-specific international admission clause before finalizing.
